name: Drive a manual transmission
blurb: Stick shift is a clutch-feel skill, learned in a car park in an afternoon and refined over a fortnight. Worth having: it makes hire cars anywhere in the world an option.
gear: A manual car and a licensed, patient supervising driver
Check your licence and insurance cover a manual first
steps: Learn the biting point with the engine running, handbrake on, no gas: lift the clutch slowly until the revs dip and the car strains.
Practise pulling away on the flat using only the clutch, no accelerator, until it is smooth.
Add a little gas and learn to balance the two pedals.
Learn to change up: lift off, clutch in, shift, clutch out smoothly while feeding the gas back in.
Learn to change down and to match engine speed so the car does not lurch.
Learn hill starts with the handbrake, then without, which is the part that actually intimidates people.
tips: Stalling is normal and harmless. Handbrake on, restart, carry on.
Riding the clutch — resting your foot on it — burns it out. Foot off the pedal entirely when not shifting.
proof: You drive a mixed route including hill starts and traffic without stalling or lurching.
